audit_methodology: MongoDB read-only via pymongo. NO write. NO delete. Owner provability checked via leader_id -> users.id match.

unsafe_docs.why_unsafe_originally: SLC-G dry-run checked only {user_id, account_id} fields; field present is leader_id (legacy single-shard ownership convention).
unsafe_docs.safety_assessment: OWNER PROVABLY RESOLVABLE via leader_id == users.id. No data loss risk if we set user_id := leader_id and account_id := leader_id (idempotent).

unsafe_docs.why_unsafe_originally: SLC-G dry-run checked only {user_id, account_id} fields; field present is leader_id pointing to a bot user (legacy seed-bot guild).
unsafe_docs.safety_assessment: OWNER PROVABLY RESOLVABLE via leader_id == users.id (bot owner). No active human player risk. Can be classified as system_seed bot-guild OR legacy_guild_missing_owner_resolvable; both safe paths.
unsafe_docs.recommended_action: SET_OWNER_FIELDS_FROM_LEADER_ID_AND_SERVER_ID_S1 (gated; requires explicit approval marker). ALTERNATIVE: mark as system_seed (also gated).

reclassification_note: Both guilds initially classified 'unsafe_unknown' in SLC-G dry-run because the simulator only checked {user_id, account_id}. Audit upgrades them to 'legacy_guild_missing_owner_resolvable'. They are NOT orphans.
af2n_impact: NONE (guilds collection is not part of AF2-N inventory/ledger).
battle_runtime_impact: NONE (guilds is not loaded by battle_engine/battle_core/combat).
